cards.name: Control-stick speed curve
cards.summary: Turns analog stick magnitude and angle into a target horizontal speed with a curved response, a floor-slope penalty and a per-form cap.
cards.behavior: The stick magnitude and angle are captured once per update and converted into a target speed and a target facing angle. In the curved response used by ground movement the first 20 magnitude units are discarded, so a light touch produces no speed at all; above that threshold the remainder drives a cosine curve whose squared output is scaled by 30 and offset by 7. The linear response, used by swimming and by scripted movement, simply multiplies magnitude by 0.8. The chosen value is then multiplied by 0.14 and reduced by 8 times the squared sine of the current floor pitch, which makes uphill movement cost speed in proportion to the terrain angle, and the result is clamped between zero and the form speed cap. One body form multiplies the target by 1.5 before the clamp. When the stick is centred the target speed is zero and the facing target falls back to the current body yaw, or to the lock-on direction while the reticle is still settling.

constants.name: Stick dead zone
constants.unit: control-stick magnitude units (full deflection reports about 64), applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Curve frequency
constants.unit: binary angle units per stick magnitude unit, evaluated per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Curve gain
constants.unit: world units/update per unit of squared cosine term, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Curve offset
constants.unit: world units/update, added per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Linear response gain
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on stick magnitude, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Straight-line conversion
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on the curve output, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Slope speed penalty
constants.unit: world units/update per unit of squared pitch sine, subtracted per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Per-form locomotion tuning
cards.summary: One 18-value tuning row per playable body supplies the run speed limit, the deceleration rate and the actor scale used for movement.
cards.behavior: Before movement runs, the current body form or movement mode selects one row of an 18-value table and copies it into the engine tuning slots: a turn deceleration scale, four further clamping scales, the deceleration rate, the run speed limit, the gravity scale, the jump impulse and a group of interaction ranges. The run limit is divided by 100 to become a world-units-per-update ceiling, so the default humanoid body tops out at 5.5, the oversized body at 3.5, the compact and aquatic bodies at 6.0 and the heavy rolling body at 6.0 with a steeper gravity scale. Any indoor room replaces the ceiling with 5.0 regardless of body. The deceleration rate is divided by 100 as well (8.0 per update squared) when speed is stepped toward zero, so releasing the stick produces a short, consistent skid. The oversized body additionally receives an actor scale of 0.015 instead of the usual 0.01, which also scales its collision volume and camera framing.

constants.name: Default-body run limit
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Oversized-body run limit
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Indoor run limit
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Deceleration rate
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update squared; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Oversized-body actor scale
constants.unit: dimensionless model-to-world scale factor, reapplied per update at 20 Hz whenever the body tuning row loads

cards.name: Pivot turn rate
cards.summary: Facing rotation when the body pivots on the spot instead of running, including the submerged reduction.
cards.behavior: When the requested facing differs from the current facing by enough that running would look wrong, the body enters a dedicated turning action, plays a looping pivot animation and steps its facing angle at 1200 binary angle units per update, roughly 6.6 degrees per update or about 132 degrees per second. When the body is submerged the same rate is multiplied by 0.5, halving the pivot speed; the same submerged factor also scales animation playback and several other water-adjusted rates so the whole body behaves as if it were moving through a heavier medium.

constants.name: Pivot rate
constants.unit: binary angle units (65536 per turn) per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Submerged rate factor
constants.unit: dimensionless multiplier on turn rate, applied per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Gravity and terminal velocity
cards.summary: Downward acceleration comes from the per-form tuning row and is clamped by a terminal velocity each update.
cards.behavior: Vertical motion adds gravity once per update and then clamps falling speed to the actor terminal velocity. Every actor starts life with a terminal velocity of 20 world units per update downward, and the player normally keeps that value, while specialised airborne actions raise or lower it for their duration. Gravity itself is read from the body tuning row and divided by 100 before use, giving 1.0 world units per update squared for the humanoid, aquatic and compact bodies, 1.4 for the heavy rolling body and 0.4 for the auxiliary row. One airborne action discards the table and applies an explicit heavier 5.5 so a launched body falls fast, and the rolling action instead derives vertical speed from the floor pitch so the body follows the terrain rather than dropping through it.

constants.name: Default-body gravity scale
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update squared; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Heavy-body gravity scale
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update squared; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Auxiliary-row gravity scale
constants.unit: hundredths of a world unit per update squared; divided by 100 before use, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Default terminal velocity
constants.unit: world units/update downward, clamped per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Forced-fall gravity
constants.unit: world units/update squared, applied per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Fall damage tiers
cards.summary: Landing from height above a threshold costs health in one of two severities and grants invulnerability updates.
cards.behavior: On landing, the accumulated fall distance is compared against 400 world units. Below that nothing is lost, although a drop above 200 units still scales a rumble request so short falls stay readable. At or above 400 units the landing applies the minor tier costing 8 health units, and at or above 800 units the major tier costing 16 health units, each with its own voice and rumble profile and each followed by a short screen quake. Both tiers grant 40 updates of invulnerability so one landing cannot be charged twice, and a lethal result ends the action immediately. Two floor types, and landings during scripted actions, zero the measured distance so those landings never hurt.

constants.unit: world units of fall distance, tested once per landing at 20 Hz

constants.name: Major tier height threshold
constants.unit: world units of fall distance, tested once per landing at 20 Hz

constants.name: Major tier health cost
constants.unit: health units (16 per heart), applied once per landing at 20 Hz

cards.name: Damage gate and invulnerability timer
cards.summary: A single signed timer decides whether incoming damage lands, and one body form quarters every hit.
cards.behavior: Damage reaches the player through 3D attack volumes that are registered against the body collider and resolved once per update. All of it funnels through one routine that first inspects the invulnerability timer: while the timer is non-zero the hit is discarded and the routine reports that nothing happened, so overlap between several volumes inside the same update cannot stack. Otherwise the amount is negated into the health field, and when the oversized form is worn the amount is shifted right twice first, quartering every hit before it is applied. The timer is stepped toward zero every update, counting up when negative and down when positive, so a scripted grace period and a damage window share the same field. Repeated contact hazards raise any positive value below 20 back to 20, which stops contact damage from ticking faster than once per second. Freeze and shock states additionally pin vertical velocity to zero and lock the body into a dedicated action until the timer runs out.

constants.name: Minimum contact invulnerability
constants.unit: updates at 20 Hz (1 s)

constants.name: Oversized-form damage shift
constants.unit: binary right shift applied to the health amount once per hit at 20 Hz

cards.name: Melee damage and combo escalation
cards.summary: Weapon damage classes, the consecutive-swing counter that upgrades the third swing, and the buffered attack window.
cards.behavior: Every melee animation indexes a damage class table. The sword class carries a normal and a strong value: 4 and 8 health units as a humanoid body, and 1 and 2 when the body is transformed, with the heavier two-handed variant reaching 4 and 8 in transformed form as well. Jumping strikes and finishers read the strong value while ordinary swings read the normal one, and the same value is written to both of the 3D attack quads that the blade sweeps through space. A counter tracks repeated swings: a different swing type or a counter already at 3 resets it, otherwise it increments, and reaching 3 rewrites the animation index two entries later in the table so the third swing of a chain becomes its finisher variant. The hostile window is set to the animation length plus 4 updates, which lets a follow-up input be buffered before the pose finishes, and each swing resets the facing angle to the body angle so an attack cannot be steered while it plays.

constants.name: Sword normal damage
constants.unit: health units (16 per heart) per swing, applied once per hit at 20 Hz

constants.name: Sword strong damage
constants.unit: health units (16 per heart) per swing, applied once per hit at 20 Hz

constants.name: Combo length
constants.unit: consecutive swings counted per attack update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Finisher table offset
constants.unit: entries skipped in the melee animation table, applied once per swing at 20 Hz

constants.name: Attack window extension
constants.unit: animation frames added to the swing length, evaluated per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Ledge detection and climb-in
cards.summary: Height and wall-angle gates for hanging, auto step-ups and full climbs onto a ledge.
cards.behavior: Wall contact is resolved into a wall normal, and the vertical gap from the feet to the ledge above that wall is kept as a distance. Three gates use it: a running climb needs at least 79 world units of clearance, a standing hang needs at least 39 units, and a low step whose climb type is the first one hops automatically after 3 updates in contact with the wall. Starting the climb action itself also requires 6 updates of wall contact unless the confirm button is pressed. The climb then subtracts 60, 59 or 41 units from the ledge distance depending on which height band the gap falls into, lifts the body 10 units above the measured gap, and snaps it down to the floor raycast below only when that floor is no more than 20 units under the placed position. The facing angle is finally set from the wall normal so the climb animation runs square to the surface.

constants.unit: world units of ledge height, tested per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Standing hang minimum
constants.unit: world units of ledge height, tested per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Slope resistance and sliding
cards.summary: Compares horizontal travel direction with the downhill direction to slow a climb or force a slide.
cards.behavior: After ground contact the floor normal is converted into a downhill yaw, and that yaw is compared with the direction the body is actually travelling. When the two directions diverge by more than 87.9 degrees, meaning the body is heading up the slope, a slowdown is derived from the vertical component of the floor normal and pushed along the downhill yaw; its step grows with the square of current speed and is never smaller than 2.2 units per update, so steep ground saps momentum progressively instead of abruptly. When the angle is below that threshold the body is treated as heading downhill: the action switches to a dedicated slide that keeps the current horizontal speed, points the facing along the downhill yaw and plays one of two slide poses depending on the surface pitch sign.

constants.name: Climb versus slide threshold
constants.unit: binary angle units (65536 per turn); 0x3E80 is 87.9 degrees, tested per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Slope slowdown scale
constants.unit: world units/update multiplied by the normal vertical deficit, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Slowdown curve gain
constants.unit: world units/update squared per unit of squared speed, per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Slowdown step floor
constants.unit: world units/update, applied per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Swim stroke timing
cards.summary: Cycle-based swimming where the target speed exists only during part of the stroke animation.
cards.behavior: While the aquatic body swims, the current animation frame decides the speed target: before frame 13 the target is zero and the body coasts, from frame 13 onward the target is 12 world units per update, and exactly on frame 13 a 16-unit impulse is written to the forward speed so the stroke visibly lunges. With no stroke animation running the idle target is 9 units per update, and facing is stepped toward the stick direction at 1600 binary angle units per update. Holding the swim input keeps the fast target; releasing it drops the body into a treading action. Vertical control is separate: the stick vertical axis is converted with a 200 scale, clamped so the body cannot rise past the surface, and the pitch is smoothed with a 4000-unit step limit so the body arcs instead of snapping between depths.

constants.name: Stroke speed target
constants.unit: world units/update, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Stroke impulse
constants.unit: world units/update added on the stroke frame, once per stroke at 20 Hz

constants.name: Idle swim speed
constants.unit: world units/update, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Stroke frame
constants.unit: animation frames of the stroke cycle, sampled per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Swim turn step
constants.unit: binary angle units (65536 per turn) per update at 20 Hz

cards.name: Body change sequence
cards.summary: A scripted action that fades, flashes, rebuilds the body and hands control back after a fixed number of updates.
cards.behavior: Changing body is not instantaneous. The worn mask selection starts a dedicated action that requests the transformation camera, aligns the body rotation with the camera direction, plays a body-specific start animation, detaches anything being carried and pins vertical velocity to zero. The action runs 0x53 updates (83) when the default body is the target and 0x37 (55) when a transformed body is, and pressing an action button after the first 5 updates skips the remainder. The commit raises a screen fill whose alpha grows by 45 per update until it exceeds 255, at which point the actor update and draw routines are swapped out for one update, the form flag is stored and the body is rebuilt on the far side. Motion blur is also enabled at a priority level during the sequence so the change reads as a flash rather than a pop.

constants.name: Default-body sequence length
constants.unit: updates at 20 Hz (83 updates, about 4.2 s)

constants.name: Transformed-body sequence length
constants.unit: updates at 20 Hz (55 updates, about 2.8 s)

constants.name: Skip window
constants.unit: updates at 20 Hz before the action can be skipped

constants.name: Fill alpha step
constants.unit: alpha units (0-255) per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Full fill alpha

cards.name: Follow camera framing
cards.summary: The default third-person camera keeps a clamped distance band, a downward pitch target and a fixed field of view, and widens that band while airborne.
cards.behavior: The normal follow camera reads a profile from a data table: a vertical offset of negative 20, a distance band of 280 to 320, a pitch target of 10 degrees, an eye position step of 22, a yaw-relative position step of 15, a yaw difference range of 40 and a field of view of 60 degrees. The band is enforced every update by clamping the distance from the focal point, so running into a wall pulls the camera in without letting it pass 320 or come closer than 280, and the vertical offset is scaled by the focal actor height so differently sized bodies frame consistently. The airborne profile keeps the same pitch target and field of view but widens the band to 240 to 340 and raises the eye step to 30 while lowering the position step to 12, which is what gives a jump a slightly pulled-back, looser framing than running.

cards.name: Lock-on camera framing
cards.summary: The battle camera interpolates between two distances by target range, closes in at low health and pulses while a swing lands.
cards.behavior: While locked onto a hostile target the camera switches to its battle profile. That profile interpolates the eye distance between 150 and 250 according to how far the locked target is, and uses a 55-degree field of view. The pitch swings between 20 and 35 degrees driven by the same distance ratio, and a dedicated parallel stage keeps both bodies inside the frame while the target moves. When the player is at or below 16 health units, that is one heart, the field of view is multiplied by 0.8 so the camera tightens as a low-health cue. While a melee weapon is being swung the field of view alternates between full and half on an 8-frame cadence, giving each connected hit a visible zoom pulse.

cards.name: Day and night clock
cards.summary: A 16-bit clock advances once per update and night is defined by two hour thresholds.
cards.behavior: The save file holds a 16-bit time-of-day value in which a full day spans 0x10000 units, so one in-game minute is about 45 units and the 24-hour clock is a fixed-point fraction of a day. Each update adds the scene time step to that value unless the game is paused, a message, cutscene, transition or the game-over state is active. Most scenes carry their own step in the scene header; the first cycle, while the instrument slot is still empty, is forced to 5 units per update, and scenes that store a zero step keep the clock frozen. Night is reported whenever the clock is at or past 18:00 or before 06:00, lighting and fog come from a table of clock ranges that divides the day into pre-dawn, morning, midday, evening and night bands, and the sky rotation is advanced from the same time step. The light direction is a 3D sun vector built from the clock: its horizontal components trace a 120-unit radius about the scene while its depth amplitude is 20, and both are scaled by 25 when the scene loads, so the light direction swings through the day rather than flipping between two states.

constants.name: Clock units per day
constants.unit: clock units (65536 per in-game day), wrapped once per day and read per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: First-cycle time step
constants.unit: clock units/update, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Night start hour
constants.unit: in-game hours on a 24-hour clock, tested per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Night end hour
constants.unit: in-game hours on a 24-hour clock, tested per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Sun orbit radius

cards.name: Clock control through instrument songs
cards.summary: Instrument effects edit the same clock: a persistent speed offset and a jump to the next day or night boundary.
cards.behavior: Time control is implemented as edits to the save clock rather than as a separate simulation. One instrument effect toggles a persistent save-level offset between zero and minus 2. The environment time-speed accessor adds that offset to the step the scene carries, and the clock integrator writes the offset in place of the raw step while a scene is advancing, so the field changes how fast the day passes instead of jumping the clock, and it survives scene changes. Another effect, confirmed through a two-choice prompt, rewrites the clock outright: if it is currently night the value jumps to 06:00, otherwise to 18:00, so it always lands exactly on the boundary being crossed, and it also clears the running countdown so the jump cannot be fatal by itself. Both edits are save-level values applied by the environment update, never resolved inside the player update.

constants.name: Slowed clock offset
constants.unit: clock units/update added to the scene step, applied per update at 20 Hz

constants.name: Night boundary target
constants.unit: in-game hours on a 24-hour clock, written once per song at 20 Hz

constants.name: Day boundary target
constants.unit: in-game hours on a 24-hour clock, written once per song at 20 Hz

cards.name: Simulation tick rate and phase order
cards.summary: Gameplay advances at a fixed divisor of the display rate, with collision phases resolved before actors.
cards.behavior: Gameplay speed is expressed as a divisor of the video frame rate rather than in seconds: the play state sets the divisor to 3, so simulation updates run at one third of the display rate, which on the original hardware means 20 updates per second. The same divisor is passed to the actor movement scale so translations authored per update stay proportionate. Other states override it, for example setting 1 while a screen-wipe tile is being prepared. Inside one gameplay tick the phases run in a fixed order: room requests, attack-versus-target collision, attack-versus-other collision, damage application and context clearing, then all actor updates, then manual and scripted cutscenes, then effects. A short freeze flash also lives in the tick: it decrements once per update, lasts 5 updates and toggles the screen fill on odd values.

constants.name: Framerate divisor
constants.unit: video frames per simulation update (20 updates per second at 60 Hz)

constants.name: Freeze flash length
constants.unit: updates at 20 Hz (0.25 s)

constants.name: Transition divisor
constants.unit: video frames per simulation update while a wipe tile is prepared, at 60 Hz
